messages.author: 068cbc8bd5fb0d5d
messages.subject: Regression on a derived parameter
parts:
I am wondering if it's possible to do a regression in NIMBLE on a derived parameter? I have mark-recapture data from 12 sites (g) and am using data augmentation to estimate the total population size (N[g]) and then density at each site (density[g]). I have measurements of forest cover and water depth at each site and wanted to do a regression to estimate how they influence the density across sites. Below is a section of the potential code (currently rough). Is there a way to do this within NIMBLE?


psi[g] ~ dunif(0, 1) # probability of an individual being in the population
beta_0 ~ dnorm(0, pow(3, -2))
beta_1 ~ dnorm(0, pow(3, -2))
beta_2 ~ dnorm(0, pow(3, -2))
 
y[i, j, g] ~ dbern(p[i, j, g]) # likelihood y = observed data for individual i, visit j, site g
p[i, j, g] <- z[i] * p0[i, j, g]
z[i, g] ~ dbern(psi[g])

# Derived parameters
N[g] <- sum(z[g,  ])
density[g] <- sum(z[g,  ]) / (xlim[g, 2] - xlim[g, 1])

# regression on derived parameter
log(density[g]) ~ dnorm(beta_0 + beta_1 * forest[g] + beta_2 * depth[g], pow(3, -2)) # Alt use poisson with N and log offset with the xlims


Thanks for any thoughts,
Dan

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Regression on a derived parameter
parts:
In general, you can't declare a deterministic node and then declare it as a stochastic node as well.  This is something some people have been interested in but is not currently supported.

In this case, I think it would work to make a vector of zeros and do

zeros[g] ~ dnorm(density[g] - (beta_0 + beta_1 * forest[g] + beta_2 * depth[g]), pow(3, -2))

In a more general case, you could write a user-defined distribution and use that to get whatever log probability contribution you need with "data" (left-hand side of a stochastic declaration) that might just be a dummy value.

-Perry
